subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should internally aborted GitHub Copilot `anthropic-messages` runs with no assistant text, tool calls, or delivery evidence be treated as model-fallback-safe, or should the fix stay at the Copilot transport/timeout layer first?
rationale: The source supports the remaining gap, but fallback after an abort can be unsafe if a side-effecting turn is still active; live Copilot behavior and maintainer policy are needed before automation chooses the repair shape.

options.title: Transport-first safe fallback
options.body: Add live proof and a Copilot transport or first-token idle failure path, then allow fallback only when the run has no tool, delivery, or replay-invalid evidence.

options.title: Broad aborted-result fallback
options.body: Classify all aborted no-output results as fallback-worthy when fallbacks are configured, accepting the replay and side-effect risk for faster recovery.

options.title: Status-only scope
options.body: Leave the current cron error classification as the only core fix and document changing the primary model away from Copilot Claude as the workaround.

recommendation.title: Transport-first safe fallback
recommendation.body: Add live proof and a Copilot transport or first-token idle failure path, then allow fallback only when the run has no tool, delivery, or replay-invalid evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision spans Copilot provider routing, stream wrapper behavior, and fallback policy, where Peter has the strongest current history signal.
